videos.caption: Going from never paying attention to what you’re eating to focusing on everything that you’re eating does suck right away and it is an adjustment, but it doesn’t have to suck forever

Eating less isn't always the answer. For years, we've been told that if we want to lose weight, we need to eat less. So we skip meals, cut portions, avoid carbs and try to get by on as little food as possible. But here's where that approach can backfire, especially in midlife. When you're constantly trying to eat less, you're often missing out on the very things that make fat loss easier to manage. Protein to help keep you full and maintain muscle. Fibre to support digestion, gut health and keep hunger in check. Food volume, so you can eat satisfying meals without consuming excessive calories. And when you're hungry all the time, it's much harder to stick to your calorie goals. You end up snacking, picking at food or overeating later in the day. The answer isn't to keep cutting calories. It's to make the calories you're eating work harder for you. Build your meals around protein, add plenty of fibre-rich foods and fill your plate with foods that give you more volume for fewer calories. You still need a calorie deficit to lose fat, but you don't need to spend your days feeling hungry and deprived. Eating smarter, not just eating less, can make all the difference.
